title: Finite direct image reflects bounded constructibility
statement:
Let $p:Z\to S$ be a
finite morphism of
Noetherian schemes and let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring.
On ordinary derived
categories of etale modules, its
derived direct image $Rp_*$
reflects membership in
$D^b_c$.

proof.text: Let F be the finite module direct image. Its exactness instance is already proved in WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Finite.Exact for ModuleCat coefficients, so no passage through a second ringed-site encoding is needed. The proved source-library F.rightDerivedFunctorHomologyFunctorIso combines exact-functor derived factorization with commutation with homology and gives, for every integer q, an isomorphism p_* H^q(K) ≅ H^q(Rp_* K). It applies to the ordinary unbounded derived category: no bounds on K are assumed.

proof.text: Use the proved source-library isZero_of_isZero_lowerStar_of_isFinite (WeilConjectures.SixFunctors.Finite.Counit), which implements the finite-stalk and conservative-geometric-stalk argument: each source stalk is a quotient of the product stalk of the image, so a zero image forces every source stalk to be zero and hence the source sheaf is zero. Unpack the bounded interval a ≤ b of Rp_* K. In every degree i with i < a or b < i, transport its zero cohomology along the comparison of Step 1 and apply reflection of zero to H^i(K). The same a,b bound K, with the identical inequality a ≤ b.

For every integer q (including those outside the bounds), the bounded-constructible predicate supplies constructibility of H^q(Rp_* K). Transport it along Step 1's isomorphism to p_* H^q(K). The private elementary helper constructible_of_iso keeps the same stratification, the same etale covers and the same finite constant module values, and composes their trivializing isomorphisms with the pullback and over-site restriction of the comparison. Apply isConstructibleEtaleModuleSheaf_of_finite_lowerStar to H^q(K), using precisely the existing finite morphism, Noetherian schemes and finite commutative ring hypotheses. Combine this degreewise constructibility with Step 2's bounds to obtain the original bounded-constructible predicate. Empty schemes and the zero coefficient ring require no case distinction; the same transported existential witnesses and bounds apply.
